newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 1.

text.p: PRAVO - The government has decided not to release any state forests to the church, leaving the final decision up to parliament.
- Industrial output increased by five percent over last August. This result is worse than the result in August, 1995 and the third lowest growth in the first eight months of this year.
- The Minister of the Environment, Jiri Skalicky, wants the costs of the renewal of the environment to be added to the price of energy.

- The parliamentary commission investigating the collapse of Kreditni banka should acknowledge that many of the mistakes made in the Czech banking sector were not the result of bad intentions, but of accounting, financial, marketing and personal inexperience according to Civic Democratic Party representative, Robert Kolar.

- Ceska Pojistovna (CP) did not take over any stock, bonds or loans from Komercni Banka other than those which were deposited in the bank according to CP's spokeswoman Marcela Doleckova. This was in response to accusations from Michal Kraus from the Czech Social Democratic Party that CP transfered over a number of lucrative loans and bonds in the days leading up to the forced administration.
- During a shareholder meeting on Monday, Banka Hana decided to increase its basic capital from 1.5 billion crowns to two billion. The increase will be through an issue of shares.

- The board of directors of the Podnikatelsky Penzejni Fond have named Ludek Dytrych as general manager. The fund is distancing itself from the SPG Group and the personnel changes are a result of this as well as a result of new shareholders in the fund.
- Poldi Ocel has founded two new subsidiary companies, Poldi Steel Corp and Poldi Steel International Sales and Marketing, in Deleware according to Poldi's general manager, Vladimir Stehlik.

- RadioMobil, one of two Czech GSM service providers, and SPT Telecom are discussing decreasing prices for connecting to Teecom's fixed telephone network according to RadioMobil's press spokeswoman, Tereza Kakosova.

- BOPO Trebic intends to extend its network of retail stores to 50 by the end of 1997 according to the shoe company's general manager, Pavel Smazil. The company currently has 30 stores, 12 of which the company owns and 18 of which are licensed.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Prague Stock Exchange's PX-50 index increased by one percentage point during trading yesterday, continuing Friday's significant growth.

- Representatives from the World Bank and the Czech Republic met in Washington on Sunday and agreed to closer cooperation in solving problems in transforming economies. The World Bank is also interested in the experience the Czech Republic had with coupon privatisation so that other countries could also use this method.
- The Czech National Bank's balance sheet total increased by five million crowns between Sept 10-20, rising to 600.85 billion crowns.

- Benzina a.s. has once again lowered the price of its petrol by 10 to 30 hellers a litre while increasing the price of diesel fuel by a similar amount. The reason for these price changes is Ceska Rafinerska's recent changes to their diesel and petrol prices.
- The amount of material investment increased in the first half of this year by more than 13 percent to 180 billion crowns.
